en: And who would this form not captivate— filled with the power of inspired eloquence arising from serene faith, and so full of majesty? (52)
The form that has been seen hundreds of times by one person,
and which another beholds for the first time—
both bring delight to their eyes.
That is equal for both as well. ||53||
For because of the incomparable nature and the gentle disposition of your body,
it brings joy at every sight.
He ordains ever-new [births] again and again. ||54||
The body is endowed with the qualities of its substratum,
and the qualities are endowed with the qualities of their presiding subjects; they are possessed of supreme perfection.
By you, who are mutually suited to one another. ||55||
Where else could these qualities of a Tathāgata be so well-established,
except in this very form of yours?
From [the body] radiant with the primary marks and secondary signs. ||56||
Your form seems to say, "I am blessed," as it proclaims the virtues of those who have taken refuge in you;
